alt: A driver mutation plus other controls still holding gives a clone in working tissue; that clone plus more drivers over decades, and several controls failing too, is what gives growth that does not end.
longDescription: Six ideas joined by five contributing links. Every link means the thing it starts from contributes to the thing it points at, so the two outcomes in the map each have more than one contributor and neither has only one. Three ideas start the map because nothing points into them: a driver mutation, other controls still hold, and several controls fail too. Two links converge on the first outcome, a clone in working tissue: one from a driver mutation, and one from other controls still hold, meaning attachment, the death programme and the response to crowding are all still working. So a single driver gives a clone and not a cancer, because the tissue's other controls are contributing to that outcome as much as the mutation is. From the clone in working tissue a link leads to more drivers over decades, a typical tumour carrying two to eight driver mutations. Two links then converge on the second outcome, growth that does not end: one from more drivers over decades, and one from several controls fail too. Read the two outcomes by comparing what feeds them. The driver mutation lies on the path to both, since it is upstream of the clone and the clone is upstream of the second outcome. What differs between the two outcomes is the third and fifth ideas: whether the tissue's other controls are still holding or have given way. That is the conclusion of the map, that the mutation alone does not select which outcome occurs.
